newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two Pakistani Sunnis held for killing 37 Shi'ites.
newsitem.headline: Two Pakistani Sunnis held for killing 37 Shi'ites.

text.p: Pakistani police said on Thursday they had arrested two Sunni Moslem militants who had admitted killing 37 Shi'ite Moslems during a spate of sectarian violence in the central province of Punjab.

"We have arrested two people who have confessed to killing 37 people belonging to the Shi'ite sect," Mushtaq Warraich, the superintendent of police in the Punjab town of Khanewal, 450 km (281 miles) from Islamabad, told Reuters by telephone.
He said Muhammad Ali, whose aliases included Cobra and Butcher, and Nadeem Khan, had been arrested after a police car chased their motorcycle on Monday.
The chase followed an attack he said the pair had carried out in the town of Shorkot earlier on Monday in which eight people, seven of them Shi'ites, had been killed in a bazaar.

Warraich said the two men, both members of the militant Sunni Lashkar-e-Jhangvi group, had planned to assassinate Sajid Naqvi, leader of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan group, at the funeral prayers for the Shorkot victims.

He said the alleged killers had also confessed to plans to murder half a dozen Shi'ite notables, including Population Welfare Minister Abida Hussain and her husband Fakhar Imam, a member of the National Assembly (lower house).
"Muhammad Ali has killed 19 Shi'ites and Nadeem killed 18 Shi'ites, and they have admitted to the murders," he said.
Warriach said both were wanted for various crimes including murder, and that Ali had a bounty of 500,000 rupees ($12,300) on his head.
"By the grace of God we have apprehended them at a time when there is tremendous pressure on the government," he said.
Violence has surged in Pakistan in recent weeks as militant Sunni and Shi'ite Moslems wage a deadly vendetta in Punjab, and rival wings of an ethnic party feud in Karachi.

Officials say more than 130 people, including religious scholars, lawyers and doctors, have been killed in Sunni-Shi'ite violence this year. Shi'ites make up about 15 percent of Pakistan's mainly Sunni population of more than 135 million.
More than 225 people have died in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi this year, compared to about 500 last year and more than 2,000 in 1995.
